verses.rationale: Follows read you-called and retains overlapping family/companion imagery.

verses.rationale: Follows read you-say and contrasts speech with conduct.

verses.rationale: Preserves historical setting and female corporate personification.

verses.rationale: Keeps frustrated divine expectation and sister witness.
verses.before: I said, ‘After she has done all these things, she will return to me.’ But she did not return. And her treacherous sister Judah saw it.
verses.after: I thought, ‘After she has done all this, she will return to me.’ But she did not return, and her treacherous sister Judah saw it.

verses.rationale: Retains pinned I-saw opening and explicit divorce metaphor.

verses.after: I saw that, although I sent faithless Israel away and gave her a divorce document because of all her adultery, her treacherous sister Judah did not fear. She too went and prostituted herself.
verses.tsw_comparator: I saw that, because of all the adulteries faithless Israel had committed, I sent her away and gave her a certificate of divorce. Yet her treacherous sister Judah was not afraid; she too went and prostituted herself.

verses.rationale: Preserves literal objects as metaphorical partners.
verses.before: Because her prostitution was so casual, she defiled the land, committing adultery with stone and wood.
verses.after: Treating her prostitution lightly, she defiled the land and committed adultery with stone and wood.
verses.tsw_comparator: Because her prostitution was so casual, she defiled the land, committing adultery with stone and wood.

verses.rationale: Keeps halfhearted return contrasted with actual repentance.
verses.before: Even after all this, her treacherous sister Judah did not return to me with all her heart, but only in falsehood,” declares the LORD.
verses.after: Despite all this, her treacherous sister Judah did not return to me with her whole heart, but only in pretense,” declares the **LORD**.
verses.tsw_comparator: Even after all this, her treacherous sister Judah did not return to me with all her heart, but only in falsehood,” declares the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserves comparative righteousness rather than absolute innocence.
verses.before: And the LORD said to me, “Faithless Israel has shown herself more righteous than treacherous Judah.
verses.after: The **LORD** said to me, “Faithless Israel has shown herself more righteous than treacherous Judah.
verses.tsw_comparator: And the LORD said to me, “Faithless Israel has shown herself more righteous than treacherous Judah.

verses.rationale: Keeps northward address and return-turning word family.

verses.rationale: Preserves confession requirement and metaphorical scattered ways.
verses.before: Only acknowledge your guilt: that you rebelled against the LORD your God, scattering your ways among strangers beneath every green tree, and that you did not listen to my voice,’ declares the LORD.

verses.tsw_comparator: Only acknowledge your guilt: that you rebelled against the LORD your God, scattering your ways among strangers beneath every green tree, and that you did not listen to my voice,’ declares the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retains husband/master ambiguity and exact gathering numbers.

verses.after: ‘Return, children who have turned away,’ declares the **LORD**, ‘for I am your husband. I will take you, one from a city and two from a clan, and bring you to Zion.
verses.tsw_comparator: ‘Return, wayward children,’ declares the LORD, ‘for I am your husband. I will take you, one from a city and two from a clan, and bring you to Zion.

verses.rationale: Keeps shepherd repetition for leaders’ task.
verses.before: I will give you shepherds after my own heart, and they will shepherd you with knowledge and understanding.
verses.after: I will give you shepherds after my own heart, and they will shepherd you with knowledge and understanding.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will give you shepherds after my own heart, and they will shepherd you with knowledge and understanding.

verses.rationale: Preserves striking disappearance of ark’s role and all negations.

verses.tsw_comparator: And when you have multiplied and been fruitful in the land in those days,” declares the LORD, “they will no longer say, ‘The ark of the covenant of the LORD.’ It will not come to mind; they will not remember it or miss it, nor will another be made.

verses.rationale: Keeps replacement throne image and nations gathering.

verses.after: At that time they will call Jerusalem the **LORD**’s Throne. All nations will gather there, to Jerusalem, for the **LORD**’s name. They will no longer follow the stubbornness of their evil hearts.
verses.tsw_comparator: At that time Jerusalem will be called the throne of the LORD, and all nations will gather to it, to the name of the LORD in Jerusalem. They will no longer walk after the stubbornness of their evil heart.

verses.rationale: Preserves two houses’ reunion and return direction.
verses.before: In those days the house of Judah will walk with the house of Israel, and together they will come from the land of the north to the land that I gave your ancestors as an inheritance.
verses.after: In those days the house of Judah will join the house of Israel. Together they will come from the northern land to the land I gave your ancestors as an inheritance.
verses.tsw_comparator: In those days the house of Judah will walk with the house of Israel, and together they will come from the land of the north to the land that I gave your ancestors as an inheritance.

verses.rationale: Follows read feminine singular address and retains sons inheritance language.
verses.before: “I myself said, ‘How I would place you among the children and give you a desirable land, the most beautiful inheritance of the nations!’ I said, ‘You will call me, “My Father,” and you will not turn away from following me.’
verses.after: I thought, “How I would place you among my sons and give you a desirable land, the most beautiful inheritance among the nations!” I thought you would call me “My Father” and would not turn away from following me.
verses.tsw_comparator: “I myself said, ‘How I would place you among the children and give you a desirable land, the most beautiful inheritance of the nations!’ And I said, ‘You will call me, “My Father,” and you will not turn away from following me.’

verses.rationale: Keeps companion term and explicit national addressee.
verses.before: But surely, as a woman betrays her companion, so you have betrayed me, house of Israel,” declares the LORD.
verses.after: But as a wife betrays her companion, so you have betrayed me, house of Israel,’ declares the **LORD**.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But surely, as a woman betrays her companion, so you have betrayed me, house of Israel,” declares the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retains former cultic heights as lament location.
verses.before: A voice is heard on the barren heights— weeping, the pleas of the children of Israel— because they have twisted their way; they have forgotten the LORD their God.
verses.after: A sound is heard on the bare heights, the weeping pleas of Israel’s children, for they have twisted their way and forgotten the **LORD** their God.
verses.tsw_comparator: A voice is heard on the barren heights— weeping, the pleas of the children of Israel— because they have twisted their way; they have forgotten the LORD their God.

verses.rationale: Marks change from summons to communal response and repeated turning.
verses.before: “Return, wayward children; I will heal your faithlessness.” “Here we are; we have come to you, for you are the LORD our God.
verses.after: “Return, children who have turned away; I will heal your turning away.” “Here we are! We come to you, for you are the **LORD** our God.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Return, wayward children; I will heal your faithlessness.” “Here we are; we have come to you, for you are the LORD our God.

verses.rationale: Retains compressed hill-uproar clause and doubled surely.
verses.before: Surely the hills are a deception, the tumult on the mountains. Surely in the LORD our God is the salvation of Israel.
verses.after: Surely the hills are a deception, the uproar on the mountains. Surely in the **LORD** our God is Israel’s salvation.
verses.tsw_comparator: Surely the hills are a deception, the tumult on the mountains. Surely in the LORD our God is the salvation of Israel.

verses.rationale: Preserves personified Shame and sacrificed human children.

verses.after: From our youth, Shame has devoured what our ancestors worked for: their flocks and cattle, their sons and daughters.

verses.rationale: Keeps collective confession’s generations and duration.

verses.rationale: Keeps agricultural preparation metaphor and specific audience.
verses.before: For thus says the LORD to the people of Judah and to Jerusalem: “Break up for yourselves unplowed ground; do not sow among thorns.
verses.after: For this is what the **LORD** says to the men of Judah and to Jerusalem: “Break up your unplowed ground; do not sow among thorns.

verses.rationale: Preserves embodied circumcision metaphor and unquenched threat.

verses.after: Circumcise yourselves to the **LORD**; remove the foreskins of your hearts, men of Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem, or my fury will burst out like fire and burn with no one to quench it, because of your evil deeds.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Circumcise yourselves to the LORD; remove the foreskins of your hearts, people of Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem, lest my wrath go out like fire and burn with no one to quench it, because of the evil of your deeds.”

verses.rationale: Keeps public alarm and collective refuge call.

verses.after: Announce in Judah, proclaim in Jerusalem: “Blow the ram’s horn through the land!” Cry out at full voice: “Gather! Let us enter the fortified cities!”
verses.tsw_comparator: Declare in Judah, and proclaim in Jerusalem; say, “Sound the ram’s horn in the land!” Cry aloud and say, “Gather yourselves, and let us go into the fortified cities!”

verses.rationale: Preserves direction, urgency and divine agency.
verses.before: Raise a signal toward Zion. Flee for safety; do not stand still, for I am bringing disaster from the north, and great destruction.
verses.after: Raise a banner toward Zion! Seek safety; do not delay! For I am bringing disaster from the north, great destruction.
verses.tsw_comparator: Raise a signal toward Zion. Flee for safety; do not stand still, for I am bringing disaster from the north, and great destruction.

verses.rationale: Keeps invader unnamed and lion comparison.
verses.before: A lion has risen from its thicket; a destroyer of nations has set out. It has gone from its place to make your land a wasteland. Your cities will be ruined, without inhabitant.
verses.after: A lion has come out of his thicket; a destroyer of nations has set out. He has left his place to devastate your land; your cities will become ruins without inhabitants.
verses.tsw_comparator: A lion has risen from its thicket; a destroyer of nations has set out. It has gone from its place to make your land a wasteland. Your cities will be ruined, without inhabitant.

verses.rationale: Preserves speaker’s inclusion in threatened us.
verses.before: For this, put on sackcloth; mourn and wail, for the burning anger of the LORD has not turned away from us.
verses.after: So put on sackcloth, mourn and howl, for the **LORD**’s burning anger has not turned away from us.
verses.tsw_comparator: For this, put on sackcloth; mourn and wail, for the burning anger of the LORD has not turned away from us.

verses.rationale: Keeps all four leadership groups.
verses.before: “And it will happen on that day,” declares the LORD, “that the heart of the king will fail, and the heart of the officials; the priests will be appalled, and the prophets astonished.”
verses.after: “On that day,” declares the **LORD**, “the king and officials will lose heart; priests will be appalled, and prophets stunned.”
verses.tsw_comparator: “And it will happen on that day,” declares the LORD, “that the heart of the king will fail, and the heart of the officials; the priests will be appalled, and the prophets astonished.”

verses.rationale: Retains prophet’s accusation of divine deception without explaining it away.

verses.after: Then I said, “Ah, Lord **GOD**! You have surely deceived this people and Jerusalem, saying, ‘You will have peace,’ while the sword reaches our very lives!”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then I said, “Ah, Lord GOD! Surely you have utterly deceived this people and Jerusalem, saying, ‘You will have peace,’ while the sword reaches to the very life.”

verses.rationale: Keeps destructive wind distinguished from useful farming wind.
verses.before: At that time it will be said to this people and to Jerusalem: “A scorching wind from the bare heights in the wilderness comes toward the daughter of my people, not for winnowing and not for cleansing.
verses.after: At that time this people and Jerusalem will be told, “A scorching wind from the wilderness’s bare heights comes toward the daughter of my people, not to winnow, not to clean—
verses.tsw_comparator: At that time it will be said to this people and to Jerusalem: “A scorching wind from the bare heights in the wilderness comes toward the daughter of my people, not for winnowing and not for cleansing.

verses.rationale: Preserves divine control and legal pronouncement.
verses.before: A wind too full for these will come at my command. Now I too will speak judgments against them.”
verses.after: a wind too strong for that comes at my command. Now I too will pronounce judgments against them.”
verses.tsw_comparator: A wind too full for these will come at my command. Now I too will speak judgments against them.”

verses.rationale: Keeps approaching enemy and quoted communal cry distinct.
verses.before: Look, he comes up like clouds; his chariots are like a storm wind. His horses are swifter than eagles. Woe to us, for we are devastated!
verses.after: Look, he rises like clouds, his chariots like a whirlwind, his horses swifter than eagles. “Woe to us! We are ruined!”
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, he comes up like clouds; his chariots are like a storm wind. His horses are swifter than eagles. Woe to us, for we are devastated!

verses.rationale: Retains cleansing and lodging imagery.
verses.before: Wash evil from your heart, Jerusalem, so that you may be saved. How long will thoughts of wickedness lodge within you?
verses.after: Wash the evil from your heart, Jerusalem, so you may be saved. How long will your harmful thoughts lodge within you?
verses.tsw_comparator: Wash evil from your heart, Jerusalem, so that you may be saved. How long will thoughts of wickedness lodge within you?

verses.rationale: Keeps approaching warning’s named geography.
verses.before: For a voice declares from Dan and announces disaster from the hill country of Ephraim.
verses.after: A voice announces news from Dan, proclaims disaster from Ephraim’s hills.
verses.tsw_comparator: For a voice declares from Dan and announces disaster from the hill country of Ephraim.

verses.rationale: Preserves watchers as siege force in context and foreign distance.
verses.before: Warn the nations: “Look! Proclaim against Jerusalem: besiegers are coming from a distant land. They raise their voices against the cities of Judah.
verses.after: “Notify the nations! Look, proclaim against Jerusalem: besiegers are coming from a distant land; they raise their voices against Judah’s cities.
verses.tsw_comparator: Warn the nations: “Look! Proclaim against Jerusalem: besiegers are coming from a distant land. They raise their voices against the cities of Judah.

verses.rationale: Keeps agricultural guard simile and feminine city.
verses.before: Like guards around a field they are against her on every side, for she has rebelled against me,” declares the LORD.
verses.after: Like guards around a field, they surround her, because she has rebelled against me,” declares the **LORD**.
verses.tsw_comparator: Like guards around a field they are against her on every side, for she has rebelled against me,” declares the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserves evil/disaster consequence and heart penetration.
verses.before: Your way and your deeds have brought this upon you. This is your evil: how bitter it is, how it reaches to your heart!
verses.after: “Your way and your deeds have brought this upon you. This is your bitter disaster; it reaches your very heart.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Your way and your deeds have brought this upon you. This is your evil: how bitter it is, how it reaches to your heart!

verses.rationale: Follows read you-heard address to soul and preserves bodily fragments.
verses.before: My inward parts, my inward parts! I writhe! The walls of my heart! My heart roars within me. I cannot be silent, for I have heard the sound of the ram’s horn, the alarm of war.
verses.after: My insides, my insides! I writhe! The walls of my heart! My heart pounds within me. I cannot keep silent, for you have heard, my soul, the ram’s horn and the battle cry.
verses.tsw_comparator: My inward parts, my inward parts! I writhe! The walls of my heart! My heart roars within me. I cannot be silent, for I have heard the sound of the ram’s horn, the alarm of war.

verses.rationale: Keeps repeated destruction and personal dwelling imagery.
verses.before: Crash upon crash is proclaimed, for all the land is devastated. Suddenly my tents are devastated, in an instant my tent curtains.
verses.after: Destruction upon destruction is announced; the whole land is devastated. Suddenly my tents are destroyed, my curtains in a moment.
verses.tsw_comparator: Crash upon crash is proclaimed, for all the land is devastated. Suddenly my tents are devastated, in an instant my tent curtains.

verses.rationale: Retains prolonged sensory alarm.
verses.before: How long must I see the signal, must I hear the sound of the ram’s horn?
verses.after: How long must I see the banner and hear the ram’s horn?
verses.tsw_comparator: How long must I see the signal, must I hear the sound of the ram’s horn?

verses.rationale: Keeps ironic wisdom and divine my-people voice.
verses.before: “For my people are foolish; they do not know me. They are foolish children, and they have no understanding. They are wise in doing evil, but they do not know how to do good.”
verses.after: “My people are foolish; they do not know me. They are senseless children without understanding. They are wise at doing evil, but do not know how to do good.”
verses.tsw_comparator: “For my people are foolish; they do not know me. They are foolish children, and they have no understanding. They are wise in doing evil, but they do not know how to do good.”

verses.rationale: Preserves Genesis creation-reversal vocabulary.
verses.before: I looked at the earth— and look: waste and emptiness; and to the heavens— and they had no light.
verses.after: I looked at the earth: it was unformed and empty; at the heavens: their light was gone.
verses.tsw_comparator: I looked at the earth— and look: waste and emptiness; and to the heavens— and they had no light.

verses.rationale: Repeats I-looked frame and two landforms.
verses.before: I looked at the mountains— and look: they were shaking; all the hills were swaying.
verses.after: I looked at the mountains: they were quaking; all the hills were shaking.
verses.tsw_comparator: I looked at the mountains— and look: they were shaking; all the hills were swaying.

verses.rationale: Keeps absence of humans and birds.
verses.before: I looked— and look: there was no human being, and every bird of the heavens had fled.
verses.after: I looked: there was no human being; all the birds of the heavens had fled.
verses.tsw_comparator: I looked— and look: there was no human being, and every bird of the heavens had fled.

verses.rationale: Preserves fourth I-looked and repeated before.
verses.before: I looked— and look: the fertile land was a wilderness, and all its cities were torn down before the LORD, before his burning anger.
verses.after: I looked: the fruitful land was wilderness; all its cities lay demolished before the **LORD**, before his burning anger.
verses.tsw_comparator: I looked— and look: the fertile land was a wilderness, and all its cities were torn down before the LORD, before his burning anger.

verses.rationale: Keeps limiting assurance within total devastation language.
verses.before: For thus says the LORD: “The whole land will become a desolation, yet I will not make a full end.
verses.after: For this is what the **LORD** says: “The whole land will become desolate, but I will not make a complete end.
verses.tsw_comparator: For thus says the LORD: “The whole land will become a desolation, yet I will not make a full end.

verses.rationale: Preserves earth mourning and irreversible declared purpose.
verses.before: Because of this the earth will mourn, and the heavens above will grow dark; for I have spoken, I have purposed. I have not relented, and I will not turn back from it.”
verses.after: For this the earth will mourn and the heavens above grow dark. I have spoken; I have resolved it. I have not relented and will not turn back.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Because of this the earth will mourn, and the heavens above will grow dark; for I have spoken, I have purposed. I have not relented, and I will not turn back from it.”

verses.rationale: Retains multiple refuges and city-person metonymy.
verses.before: At the sound of horseman and archer every city flees. They enter the thickets and climb among the rocks. Every city is abandoned, and no one lives in them.
verses.after: At the sound of horsemen and archers, every city flees. They enter thickets and climb among rocks. Every city is abandoned; not a person lives in them.
verses.tsw_comparator: At the sound of horseman and archer every city flees. They enter the thickets and climb among the rocks. Every city is abandoned, and no one lives in them.

verses.rationale: Keeps cosmetics and lethal reversal of lovers.
verses.before: And you, devastated one, what will you do? Though you dress in scarlet, though you adorn yourself with ornaments of gold, though you enlarge your eyes with antimony, in vain you make yourself beautiful. Your lovers reject you; they seek your life.
verses.after: And you, devastated one, what are you doing? Though you dress in scarlet and adorn yourself with gold, though you widen your eyes with dark paint, you make yourself beautiful for nothing. Your lovers despise you; they seek your life.
verses.tsw_comparator: And you, devastated one, what will you do? Though you dress in scarlet, though you adorn yourself with ornaments of gold, though you enlarge your eyes with antimony, in vain you make yourself beautiful. Your lovers reject you; they seek your life.

verses.rationale: Preserves first childbirth and explicit attackers.
verses.before: For I hear a voice like that of a woman in labor, distress like that of one giving birth to her first child— the voice of Daughter Zion, gasping for breath, spreading out her hands: “Woe is me! For my life grows faint before killers.”
verses.after: I hear a voice like a woman in labor, distress like one bearing her first child— the voice of Daughter Zion, gasping, spreading out her hands: “Woe to me! My life is failing before killers!”
verses.tsw_comparator: For I hear a voice like that of a woman in labor, distress like that of one giving birth to her first child— the voice of Daughter Zion, gasping for breath, spreading out her hands: “Woe is me! For my life grows faint before killers.”

verses.rationale: Keeps single righteous person condition and female city pardon.
verses.before: Roam through the streets of Jerusalem; look, please, and take note. Search her squares: if you can find anyone, if there is one who does justice, who seeks faithfulness, then I will forgive her.
verses.after: “Roam Jerusalem’s streets; look and find out! Search her squares. If you find one person who does justice and seeks faithfulness, I will forgive her.
verses.tsw_comparator: Roam through the streets of Jerusalem; look, please, and take note. Search her squares: if you can find anyone, if there is one who does justice, who seeks faithfulness, then I will forgive her.

verses.rationale: Preserves misuse of correct oath formula.
verses.before: Though they say, “As the LORD lives,” they swear falsely.
verses.after: Even when they say, ‘As the **LORD** lives,’ they swear falsely.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Though they say, “As the LORD lives,” they swear falsely.

verses.rationale: Keeps physical resistance and repeated refusal.
verses.before: LORD, are not your eyes upon faithfulness? You struck them, but they did not grieve; you brought them to an end, but they refused to receive discipline. They made their faces harder than rock; they refused to turn back.
verses.after: **LORD**, do your eyes not look for faithfulness? You struck them, but they felt no pain; you consumed them, but they refused discipline. They made their faces harder than rock and refused to return.
verses.tsw_comparator: LORD, are not your eyes upon faithfulness? You struck them, but they did not grieve; you brought them to an end, but they refused to receive discipline. They made their faces harder than rock; they refused to turn back.

verses.rationale: Marks observer’s hypothesis rather than narrator-endorsed generalization about poverty.
verses.before: Then I said, “Surely these are only the poor; they have acted foolishly, for they do not know the way of the LORD, the justice of their God.
verses.after: I thought, “These are only the poor; they act foolishly because they do not know the **LORD**’s way, their God’s judgment.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then I said, “Surely these are only the poor; they have acted foolishly, for they do not know the way of the LORD, the justice of their God.

verses.rationale: Keeps elite failure overturning initial hypothesis.
verses.before: I will go to the great and speak with them, for they know the way of the LORD, the justice of their God.” But they too, together, had broken the yoke; they had torn off the bonds.
verses.after: Let me go to the great and speak with them, for they know the **LORD**’s way, their God’s judgment.” But together they too had broken the yoke and torn apart the bonds.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will go to the great and speak with them, for they know the way of the LORD, the justice of their God.” But they too, together, had broken the yoke; they had torn off the bonds.

verses.rationale: Retains three predators and violent consequence.
verses.before: So a lion from the forest will strike them; a wolf of the desert plains will devastate them. A leopard watches over their cities; everyone who goes out from them will be torn apart. For their rebellions are many; their turnings away are great.
verses.after: So a lion from the forest will strike them, a wolf from the deserts will devastate them, and a leopard will watch their cities. Everyone leaving them will be torn apart, for their rebellions are many and their turning away is great.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore a lion from the forest will strike them; a wolf of the desert plains will devastate them. A leopard watches over their cities; everyone who goes out from them will be torn apart. For their rebellions are many; their turnings away are great.

verses.rationale: Keeps divine provision and unfaithful response.
verses.before: “Why should I forgive you? Your children have forsaken me and have sworn by what is not God. I satisfied them, and they committed adultery; they crowd into the house of a prostitute.
verses.after: “How can I forgive you? Your children abandoned me and swore by what are not gods. I fed them fully, but they committed adultery and crowded into a prostitute’s house.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Why should I forgive you? Your children have forsaken me and have sworn by what is not God. I satisfied them, and they committed adultery; they crowd into the house of a prostitute.

verses.rationale: Preserves animal sexual metaphor and specific wives.
verses.before: They are well-fed, lustful stallions; each person neighs after the wife of a neighbor.
verses.after: They were well-fed, lustful stallions, each neighing after his neighbor’s wife.
verses.tsw_comparator: They are well-fed, lustful stallions; each one neighs after the wife of a neighbor.

verses.rationale: Establishes repeated judicial question refrain.
verses.before: Should I not punish for these things?” declares the LORD. “Should I not take vengeance on a nation like this?”
verses.after: Should I not call them to account for this?” declares the **LORD**. “Should I not take vengeance on a nation like this?
verses.tsw_comparator: Should I not punish for these things?” declares the LORD. “Should I not take vengeance on a nation like this?”

verses.rationale: Chooses vineyard reading from shoots context; wall alternative noted.
verses.before: “Go up among her vine rows and destroy, but do not make a full end. Strip away her branches, for they do not belong to the LORD.
verses.after: Climb through her vine rows and destroy, but do not make a complete end. Strip off her shoots, for they do not belong to the **LORD**.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Go up among her vine rows and destroy, but do not make a full end. Strip away her branches, for they do not belong to the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserves both houses and emphatic betrayal.
verses.before: For the house of Israel and the house of Judah have utterly betrayed me,” declares the LORD.
verses.after: For the house of Israel and the house of Judah have thoroughly betrayed me,” declares the **LORD**.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the house of Israel and the house of Judah have utterly betrayed me,” declares the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keeps ambiguous denial wording rather than categorical atheism.
verses.before: They have denied LORD and said, “He is nothing. No evil will come upon us; we will not see sword or famine.
verses.after: They have denied the **LORD**, saying, “It is not he! Disaster will not come upon us; we will see neither sword nor famine.
verses.tsw_comparator: They have denied LORD and said, “He is nothing. No evil will come upon us; we will not see sword or famine.

verses.rationale: Retains hostile assessment of prophets and retaliatory wish.
verses.before: The prophets will become wind, and the word is not in them. Thus it will be done to them.”
verses.after: The prophets will become wind; the word is not in them. Let this happen to them!”
verses.tsw_comparator: The prophets will become wind, and the word is not in them. Thus it will be done to them.”

verses.rationale: Keeps plural accusers to singular prophet shift and word-fire image.
verses.before: So, thus says the LORD, God of hosts: “Because you speak this word, look, I am making my words fire in your mouth, and this people wood; the fire will consume them.
verses.after: So this is what the **LORD**, God of hosts, says: “Because you have said this, look, I am making my words in your mouth fire and this people wood. The fire will consume them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore, thus says the LORD, God of hosts: “Because you speak this word, look, I am making my words fire in your mouth, and this people wood; the fire will consume them.

verses.rationale: Preserves repeated nation and incomprehensible language.
verses.before: Look, I am bringing against you a nation from far away, house of Israel,” declares the LORD. “It is an enduring nation; it is a nation from ancient time. It is a nation whose language you do not know, and you will not understand what it speaks.
verses.after: Look, I am bringing a nation from far away against you, house of Israel,” declares the **LORD**. “It is an enduring nation, an ancient nation, a nation whose language you do not know, whose speech you cannot understand.
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, I am bringing against you a nation from far away, house of Israel,” declares the LORD. “It is an enduring nation; it is a nation from ancient time. It is a nation whose language you do not know, and you will not understand what it speaks.

verses.rationale: Retains deadly quiver metaphor.
verses.before: Its quiver is like an open grave; all of them are warriors.
verses.after: Its quiver is an open grave; all its men are warriors.
verses.tsw_comparator: Its quiver is like an open grave; all of them are warriors.

verses.rationale: Preserves repeated devour and children as objects rather than harmonizing syntax to food-only loss.
verses.before: It will consume your harvest and your bread; they will consume your sons and your daughters. It will consume your flock and your herd; it will consume your vine and your fig tree. With the sword it will crush your fortified cities in which you trust.
verses.after: It will devour your harvest and your bread, devour your sons and daughters, devour your flocks and cattle, devour your vines and fig trees. With the sword it will shatter the fortified cities you trust.
verses.tsw_comparator: It will consume your harvest and your bread; they will consume your sons and your daughters. It will consume your flock and your herd; it will consume your vine and your fig tree. With the sword it will crush your fortified cities in which you trust.

verses.rationale: Keeps repeated limitation on destruction.
verses.before: “But even in those days,” declares the LORD, “I will not make a full end of you.
verses.after: Yet even in those days,” declares the **LORD**, “I will not make a complete end of you.
verses.tsw_comparator: “But even in those days,” declares the LORD, “I will not make a full end of you.

verses.rationale: Preserves service-for-service reversal and land contrast.
verses.before: And when you ask, ‘Why has the LORD our God done all these things to us?’ then you will say to them, ‘As you forsook me and served foreign gods in your land, so you will serve strangers in a land that is not yours.’
verses.after: “When you ask, ‘Why has the **LORD** our God done all this to us?’ tell them, ‘As you abandoned me and served foreign gods in your own land, so you will serve foreigners in a land not your own.’
verses.tsw_comparator: And when you ask, ‘Why has the LORD our God done all these things to us?’ then you shall say to them, ‘As you forsook me and served foreign gods in your land, so you will serve strangers in a land that is not yours.’

verses.rationale: Keeps named audience and herald formula.
verses.before: Declare this in the house of Jacob; proclaim it in Judah, saying:
verses.after: “Announce this in the house of Jacob; proclaim it in Judah:
verses.tsw_comparator: Declare this in the house of Jacob; proclaim it in Judah, saying:

verses.rationale: Retains paired unused faculties.
verses.before: “Hear this, please, foolish people without understanding, who have eyes but do not see, who have ears but do not hear.
verses.after: ‘Hear this, foolish people without sense, who have eyes but do not see, ears but do not hear.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Hear this, please, foolish people without understanding, who have eyes but do not see, who have ears but do not hear.

verses.rationale: Keeps repeated cannot-cross and humble sand boundary.
verses.before: Will you not fear me?” declares the LORD. “Will you not tremble before me—I who set the sand as a boundary for the sea, an enduring decree that it cannot cross? Though its waves rage, they cannot prevail; though they roar, they cannot cross it.
verses.after: Do you not fear me?’ declares the **LORD**. ‘Will you not tremble before me, who set sand as the sea’s boundary, an everlasting limit it cannot cross? Its waves surge, but cannot prevail; they roar, but cannot cross it.
verses.tsw_comparator: Will you not fear me?” declares the LORD. “Will you not tremble before me—I who set the sand as a boundary for the sea, an enduring decree that it cannot cross? Though its waves rage, they cannot prevail; though they roar, they cannot cross it.

verses.rationale: Contrasts human rebellion with bounded sea.
verses.before: But this people has a stubborn and rebellious heart. They have turned aside and gone away.
verses.after: But this people has a stubborn, rebellious heart; they turned aside and went away.
verses.tsw_comparator: But this people has a stubborn and rebellious heart. They have turned aside and gone away.

verses.rationale: Preserves seasonal rains and harvest weeks.
verses.before: They do not say in their heart, ‘Let us fear the LORD our God, who gives rain—the early rain and the latter rain—in its season, who keeps for us the appointed weeks of harvest.’
verses.after: They do not say in their hearts, “Let us fear the **LORD** our God, who gives rain in its season, autumn and spring rain, and keeps for us the appointed weeks of harvest.”
verses.tsw_comparator: They do not say in their heart, ‘Let us fear the LORD our God, who gives rain—the early rain and the latter rain—in its season, who keeps for us the appointed weeks of harvest.’

verses.rationale: Keeps consequences linked to preceding agricultural gifts.
verses.before: Your iniquities have turned these away, and your sins have withheld good from you.
verses.after: Your offenses have turned these away; your sins have kept good things from you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Your iniquities have turned these away, and your sins have withheld good from you.

verses.rationale: Preserves difficult hunter simile and human prey.
verses.before: For wicked people are found among my people. They watch, crouching like bird-catchers; they set a destructive trap; they catch people.
verses.after: For wicked people are found among my people. They lie in wait like crouching birdcatchers; they set a trap and catch human beings.
verses.tsw_comparator: For wicked people are found among my people. They watch, crouching like bird-catchers; they set a destructive trap; they catch people.

verses.rationale: Keeps wealth attributed to trapping/deception.
verses.before: Like a cage full of birds, so their houses are full of deceit. Therefore they have become great and rich.
verses.after: Like a cage full of birds, their houses are full of deceit. That is how they became great and rich.
verses.tsw_comparator: Like a cage full of birds, so their houses are full of deceit. Therefore they have become great and rich.

verses.rationale: Retains bodily prosperity and two denied legal protections.
verses.before: They have grown fat; they are sleek. They have gone beyond deeds of evil. They do not judge the case—the case of the orphan—yet they prosper; and they do not uphold the justice of the needy.
verses.after: They have grown fat and sleek; their evil knows no bounds. They do not judge the orphan’s case to secure justice, and they do not defend the poor person’s rights.
verses.tsw_comparator: They have grown fat; they are sleek. They have gone beyond deeds of evil. They do not judge the case—the case of the orphan—yet they prosper; and they do not uphold the justice of the needy.

verses.rationale: Repeats 5:9 refrain exactly in substance.
verses.before: Should I not punish for these things?” declares the LORD. “Should I not take vengeance on a nation like this?”
verses.after: Should I not call them to account for this?’ declares the **LORD**. ‘Should I not take vengeance on a nation like this?’
verses.tsw_comparator: Should I not punish for these things?” declares the LORD. “Should I not take vengeance on a nation like this?”

verses.rationale: Keeps double horror introduction.
verses.before: A shocking and horrible thing has happened in the land:
verses.after: “An appalling, horrible thing has happened in the land:
verses.tsw_comparator: A shocking and horrible thing has happened in the land:

verses.rationale: Preserves complicity of people and uncertain priest-prophet relation.
verses.before: The prophets prophesy falsely, and the priests rule by their own authority; and my people love it so. But what will you do when its end comes?
verses.after: prophets prophesy falsely, priests rule at their direction, and my people love it this way. But what will you do when the end comes?”
verses.tsw_comparator: The prophets prophesy falsely, and the priests rule by their own authority; and my people love it so. But what will you do when its end comes?

verses.rationale: Keeps flight from city rather than into it and all place names.
verses.before: Flee for safety, people of Benjamin, from within Jerusalem! Blow the trumpet in Tekoa; raise a signal over Beth-haccherem, for disaster looks out from the north— a great destruction.
verses.after: Seek safety, people of Benjamin, away from Jerusalem! Blow the ram’s horn in Tekoa; raise a signal over Beth-haccherem. For disaster looms from the north, great destruction.
verses.tsw_comparator: Flee for safety, people of Benjamin, from within Jerusalem! Blow the trumpet in Tekoa; raise a signal over Beth-haccherem, for disaster looks out from the north— a great destruction.

verses.rationale: Chooses destroy sense of difficult verb; comparison alternative noted.
verses.before: The lovely and delicate one— Daughter Zion—I will destroy.
verses.after: I will destroy Daughter Zion, beautiful and pampered.
verses.tsw_comparator: The lovely and delicate one— Daughter Zion—I will destroy.

verses.rationale: Preserves invaders as pastoral encampment.
verses.before: Shepherds will come against her with their flocks; they will pitch their tents around her. Each will pasture his own portion.
verses.after: Shepherds with their flocks will come against her; they will pitch tents all around her, each grazing his own patch.
verses.tsw_comparator: Shepherds will come against her with their flocks; they will pitch their tents around her. Each will pasture his own portion.

verses.rationale: Keeps holy-war preparation and attackers’ urgency.
verses.before: “Prepare war against her! Rise up, and let us attack at noon!” “Woe to us, for the day is turning; for the shadows of evening are lengthening.”
verses.after: “Consecrate war against her! Rise, let us attack at noon! Alas for us, the day is declining; evening shadows are lengthening.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Prepare war against her! Rise up, and let us attack at noon!” “Woe to us, for the day is turning; for the shadows of evening are lengthening.”

verses.rationale: Retains shift to night attack.
verses.before: “Rise up, and let us attack by night and destroy her strongholds!”
verses.after: Rise, let us attack at night and destroy her palaces!”
verses.tsw_comparator: “Rise up, and let us attack by night and destroy her strongholds!”

verses.rationale: Preserves divine order for siege and civic oppression charge.
verses.before: For this is what the LORD of Hosts says: “Cut down her trees and heap up a siege ramp against Jerusalem. This is the city that must be punished; within her there is nothing but oppression.
verses.after: For this is what the **LORD** of hosts says: “Cut down trees and heap a siege ramp against Jerusalem. This is the city to be called to account; there is nothing but oppression within her.
verses.tsw_comparator: For this is what the LORD of Hosts says: “Cut down her trees and heap up a siege ramp against Jerusalem. This is the city that must be punished; within her there is nothing but oppression.

verses.rationale: Keeps sustained evil-water image and physical injuries.
verses.before: As a well keeps its water cool, so she keeps her wickedness fresh. Violence and devastation are heard within her; before me are sickness and wounds continually.
verses.after: As a well keeps its water flowing, so she keeps her wickedness flowing. Violence and devastation are heard in her; sickness and wounds are constantly before me.
verses.tsw_comparator: As a well keeps its water cool, so she keeps her wickedness fresh. Violence and devastation are heard within her; before me are sickness and wounds continually.

verses.rationale: Preserves conditional warning and relational withdrawal.
verses.before: Be warned, Jerusalem, lest my soul turn away from you; lest I make you a desolation, an uninhabited land.”
verses.after: Accept correction, Jerusalem, or I will turn away from you and make you desolate, a land without inhabitants.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Be warned, Jerusalem, lest my soul turn away from you; lest I make you a desolation, an uninhabited land.”

verses.rationale: Keeps repeated gleaning of remnant and difficult branch/basket term.
verses.before: This is what the LORD of Hosts says: “They will thoroughly glean the remnant of Israel like a vine. Pass your hand again over the branches like one gathering grapes.”
verses.after: This is what the **LORD** of hosts says: “They will thoroughly glean Israel’s remnant like a vine. Pass your hand over the branches again, like a grape gatherer.”
verses.tsw_comparator: This is what the LORD of Hosts says: “They will thoroughly glean the remnant of Israel like a vine. Pass your hand again over the branches like one gathering grapes.”

verses.rationale: Preserves circumcision image applied to hearing.
verses.before: To whom can I speak and give warning, that they may listen? Look—their ear is uncircumcised, and they are unable to pay attention. Look—the word of the LORD has become an object of scorn to them; they take no pleasure in it.
verses.after: To whom can I speak and give warning so they will listen? Their ears are uncircumcised; they cannot pay attention. The **LORD**’s word is an insult to them; they take no pleasure in it.
verses.tsw_comparator: To whom can I speak and give warning, that they may listen? Look—their ear is uncircumcised, and they are unable to pay attention. Look—the word of the LORD has become an object of scorn to them; they take no pleasure in it.

verses.rationale: Marks command after prophet’s complaint and retains vulnerable victims.
verses.before: Yet I am full of the wrath of the LORD; I am weary of holding it in. “Pour it out on the child in the street and on the gathering of young men together. For man and woman alike will be taken, the old and those full of days.
verses.after: I am filled with the **LORD**’s fury; I am weary of holding it in. “Pour it out on children in the street and on gatherings of young men, for husband and wife alike will be captured, the old and those full of years.
verses.tsw_comparator: But I am full of the wrath of the LORD; I am weary of holding it in. “Pour it out on the child in the street and on the gathering of young men together. For man and woman alike will be taken, the old and those full of days.

verses.rationale: Preserves wives seized with property as real harm, not abstract loss.
verses.before: Their houses will be turned over to others, along with their fields and wives, for I will stretch out my hand against the inhabitants of the land,” declares the LORD.
verses.after: Their houses will pass to others, together with fields and wives, for I will stretch out my hand against the land’s inhabitants,” declares the **LORD**.
verses.tsw_comparator: Their houses will be turned over to others, along with their fields and wives, for I will stretch out my hand against the inhabitants of the land,” declares the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keeps two comprehensive ranges.
verses.before: “For from the least of them to the greatest of them, everyone is greedy for gain; from prophet to priest, everyone deals falsely.
verses.after: “From the least to the greatest, all are greedy for gain. From prophet to priest, all practice falsehood.
verses.tsw_comparator: “For from the least of them to the greatest of them, everyone is greedy for gain; from prophet to priest, everyone deals falsely.

verses.rationale: Preserves medical severity and doubled false assurance.
verses.before: They have treated the wound of my people lightly, saying, ‘Peace, peace,’ when there is no peace.
verses.after: They treat my people’s fracture as a trifling wound, saying, ‘Peace, peace,’ when there is no peace.
verses.tsw_comparator: They have treated the wound of my people lightly, saying, ‘Peace, peace,’ when there is no peace.

verses.rationale: Keeps rhetorical shame question and falling/stumbling parallel.
verses.before: Were they ashamed because they committed an abomination? No, they were not ashamed at all; they did not even know how to blush. So they will fall among people who fall; at the time when I punish them, they will stumble,” says the LORD.
verses.after: Were they ashamed of the offensive things they did? No, they felt no shame; they did not know how to blush. So they will fall among the fallen; when I call them to account, they will stumble,” says the **LORD**.
verses.tsw_comparator: Were they ashamed because they committed an abomination? No, they were not ashamed at all; they did not even know how to blush. Therefore they will fall among those who fall; at the time when I punish them, they will stumble,” says the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retains path search and explicit refusal without generic traditionalism.
verses.before: This is what the LORD says: “Stand at the crossroads and see; ask for the ancient paths: Where is the good way? Walk in it, and find rest for yourselves.” But they said, “We will not walk in it.”
verses.after: This is what the **LORD** says: “Stand at the crossroads and look. Ask about the ancient paths: where is the good way? Walk in it, and find rest for yourselves. But they said, ‘We will not walk in it.’
verses.tsw_comparator: This is what the LORD says: “Stand at the crossroads and see; ask for the ancient paths: Where is the good way? Walk in it, and find rest for yourselves.” But they said, “We will not walk in it.”

verses.rationale: Preserves warning and matching refusal.
verses.before: I set watchmen over you: “Pay attention to the sound of the trumpet!” But they said, “We will not pay attention.”
verses.after: I stationed watchmen over you: ‘Pay attention to the ram’s horn!’ But they said, ‘We will not pay attention.’
verses.tsw_comparator: I set watchmen over you: “Pay attention to the sound of the trumpet!” But they said, “We will not pay attention.”

verses.rationale: Keeps difficult assembly address rather than silently emending.
verses.before: So hear, nations; know, congregation, what will happen to them.
verses.after: So hear, nations; know, assembly, what is among them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore hear, nations; know, congregation, what will happen to them.

verses.rationale: Preserves disaster as thought-fruit and rejected instruction.
verses.before: Hear, earth! Look, I am bringing disaster on this people, the fruit of their plans, because they have not paid attention to my words and have rejected my instruction.
verses.after: Hear, earth! Look, I am bringing disaster on this people, the fruit of their thoughts, because they did not attend to my words and rejected my instruction.
verses.tsw_comparator: Hear, earth! Look, I am bringing disaster on this people, the fruit of their plans, because they have not paid attention to my words and have rejected my instruction.

verses.rationale: Keeps costly imported ingredients contrasted with rejected worship.
verses.before: What use to me is frankincense that comes from Sheba, or the finest cane from a distant land? Your burnt offerings are not acceptable, and your sacrifices do not please me.
verses.after: What use to me is frankincense from Sheba or fine aromatic cane from a distant land? Your burnt offerings are not acceptable; your sacrifices do not please me.”
verses.tsw_comparator: What use to me is frankincense that comes from Sheba, or the finest cane from a distant land? Your burnt offerings are not acceptable, and your sacrifices do not please me.

verses.rationale: Retains divine placed obstacles and intergenerational harm.
verses.before: So this is what the LORD says: “Look, I am placing stumbling blocks before this people; parents and children alike will stumble over them; neighbor and friend will perish.”
verses.after: So this is what the **LORD** says: “Look, I am placing obstacles before this people. Parents and children together will stumble over them; neighbors and companions will perish.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore this is what the LORD says: “Look, I am placing stumbling blocks before this people; parents and children alike will stumble over them; neighbor and friend will perish.”

verses.rationale: Keeps invader unnamed and distant origin.
verses.before: This is what the LORD says: “Look, a people is coming from a northern land; a great nation is roused from the farthest parts of the earth.
verses.after: This is what the **LORD** says: “Look, a people comes from the northern land; a great nation is stirred up from earth’s farthest reaches.
verses.tsw_comparator: This is what the LORD says: “Look, a people is coming from a northern land; a great nation is roused from the farthest parts of the earth.

verses.rationale: Preserves weapons, cruelty and sea-roar simile.
verses.before: They take hold of bow and javelin. They are cruel and show no compassion. Their sound roars like the sea, and they ride on horses, drawn up as one man for battle against you, Daughter Zion.”
verses.after: They grip bow and javelin; they are cruel and show no compassion. Their voice roars like the sea; they ride horses, arrayed for battle against you, Daughter Zion.”
verses.tsw_comparator: They take hold of bow and javelin. They are cruel and show no compassion. Their sound roars like the sea, and they ride on horses, drawn up as one man for battle against you, Daughter Zion.”

verses.rationale: Keeps communal reaction and labor pains.
verses.before: “We have heard its report; our hands have gone limp. Anguish has seized us, pain like that of a woman in labor.”
verses.after: We have heard the report of them; our hands hang limp. Distress has seized us, pain like a woman giving birth.
verses.tsw_comparator: “We have heard its report; our hands have gone limp. Anguish has seized us, pain like that of a woman in labor.”

verses.rationale: Follows read plural commands and retains recurring terror phrase.
verses.before: Do not go out into the field, and do not walk on the road, for the enemy has a sword— terror is on every side.
verses.after: Do not go into the fields or walk along the road, for the enemy has a sword— terror on every side!
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not go out into the field, and do not walk on the road, for the enemy has a sword— terror is on every side.

verses.rationale: Keeps singular daughter and speaker included in us.
verses.before: Daughter of my people, put on sackcloth and roll in ashes. Mourn as for an only child; make bitter lamentation, for suddenly the destroyer will come against us.
verses.after: Daughter of my people, put on sackcloth and roll in ashes. Mourn as for an only child; raise a bitter lament, for suddenly the destroyer will come upon us.
verses.tsw_comparator: Daughter of my people, put on sackcloth and roll in ashes. Mourn as for an only child; make bitter lamentation, for suddenly the destroyer will come against us.

verses.rationale: Preserves pinned fortress in mixed metallurgical context; alternative ore noted.
verses.before: “I have made you an assayer among my people, a fortress, that you may know and test their way.
verses.after: “I have made you an assayer among my people, a fortress, so you may know and test their way.
verses.tsw_comparator: “I have made you an assayer among my people, a fortress, that you may know and test their way.

verses.rationale: Keeps base-metal identities and universal indictment.
verses.before: All of them are the most stubborn rebels, going about as slanderers. They are bronze and iron; all of them act corruptly.
verses.after: They are all stubborn rebels, going about as slanderers, bronze and iron; all are corrupt.
verses.tsw_comparator: All of them are the most stubborn rebels, going about as slanderers. They are bronze and iron; all of them act corruptly.

verses.rationale: Follows read fire-consumed division and preserves failed refining.
verses.before: The bellows burn fiercely; the lead is consumed by the fire. In vain they keep refining, but the wicked are not removed.
verses.after: The bellows blow fiercely; the lead is consumed by fire. The refiner refines for nothing; the wicked are not separated out.
verses.tsw_comparator: The bellows burn fiercely; the lead is consumed by the fire. In vain they keep refining, but the wicked are not removed.

verses.rationale: Keeps rejected/rejected naming explanation.
verses.before: They call them rejected silver, for the LORD has rejected them.”
verses.after: They are called Rejected Silver, for the **LORD** has rejected them.”
verses.tsw_comparator: They call them rejected silver, for the LORD has rejected them.”

verses.rationale: Preserves third-person narrative reset.
verses.before: The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD:
verses.after: The word that came to Jeremiah from the **LORD**:
verses.tsw_comparator: The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD:

verses.rationale: Keeps temple threshold audience and all three divine names.
verses.before: “Stand at the gate of the house of the LORD, and proclaim there this word. Say: Hear the word of the LORD, all Judah, you who enter these gates to worship the LORD.
verses.after: “Stand at the gate of the **LORD**’s house and proclaim this word there: ‘Hear the **LORD**’s word, all you of Judah who enter these gates to bow before the **LORD**.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Stand at the gate of the house of the LORD, and proclaim there this word. Say: Hear the word of the LORD, all Judah, you who enter these gates to worship the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keeps conditional residence and behavior change; dwell-with alternative noted.
verses.before: Thus says the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel: Make your ways and your deeds good, and I will let you dwell in this place.
verses.after: This is what the **LORD** of hosts, Israel’s God, says: Put your ways and deeds right, and I will let you live in this place.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus says the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel: Make your ways and your deeds good, and I will let you dwell in this place.

verses.rationale: Preserves triple formula and plural demonstrative.
verses.before: Do not trust in deceptive words, saying, ‘The temple of the LORD, the temple of the LORD, the temple of the LORD—these are.’
verses.after: Do not trust deceptive words: “The **LORD**’s temple! The **LORD**’s temple! These are the **LORD**’s temple!”
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not trust in deceptive words, saying, ‘The temple of the LORD, the temple of the LORD, the temple of the LORD—these are.’

verses.rationale: Keeps emphatic if and interpersonal justice.
verses.before: For if you truly make your ways and your deeds good; if you truly do justice between one person and another;
verses.after: If you truly put your ways and deeds right, if you truly do justice between one person and another,
verses.tsw_comparator: For if you truly make your ways and your deeds good; if you truly do justice between one person and another;

verses.rationale: Preserves all protected groups and concrete harms.
verses.before: if you do not oppress the resident alien, the orphan, or the widow; if you do not shed innocent blood in this place; and if you do not go after other gods, to your own harm,
verses.after: if you do not oppress the resident foreigner, the orphan or the widow, do not shed innocent blood in this place, and do not follow other gods to your own harm,
verses.tsw_comparator: if you do not oppress the resident alien, the orphan, or the widow; if you do not shed innocent blood in this place; and if you do not go after other gods, to your own harm,

verses.rationale: Keeps land inheritance and temporal scope.
verses.before: then I will let you dwell in this place, in the land that I gave to your ancestors from age to age.
verses.after: then I will let you live in this place, in the land I gave your ancestors from long ago and forever.
verses.tsw_comparator: then I will let you dwell in this place, in the land that I gave to your ancestors from age to age.

verses.rationale: Retains accusation after conditional promise.
verses.before: Look, you are trusting in deceptive words that bring no benefit.
verses.after: But look, you trust deceptive words that cannot help.
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, you are trusting in deceptive words that bring no benefit.

verses.rationale: Preserves six charges with named Baal.
verses.before: Will you steal, murder, commit adultery, swear falsely, burn incense to Baal, and go after other gods whom you have not known,
verses.after: Will you steal, murder, commit adultery, swear falsely, burn offerings to Baal and follow other gods you have not known,
verses.tsw_comparator: Will you steal, murder, commit adultery, swear falsely, burn incense to Baal, and go after other gods whom you have not known,

verses.rationale: Keeps sanctuary refuge enabling further wrongdoing.
verses.before: then come and stand before me in this house that is called by my name, and say, ‘We are delivered,’ so that you may do all these detestable things?
verses.after: then come and stand before me in this house that bears my name, and say, “We are safe!”—only to go on doing all these offensive things?
verses.tsw_comparator: then come and stand before me in this house that is called by my name, and say, ‘We are delivered,’ so that you may do all these detestable things?

verses.rationale: Preserves robbers’ refuge image and divine witness.
verses.before: Has this house that is called by my name become, in your eyes, a den of robbers? Even I myself have seen it, declares the LORD.
verses.after: Has this house that bears my name become a robbers’ den in your eyes? Look, I too have seen it,’ declares the **LORD**.
verses.tsw_comparator: Has this house that is called by my name become, in your eyes, a den of robbers? Even I myself have seen it, declares the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keeps historical sanctuary comparison without adding archaeology.
verses.before: But go now to my place that was in Shiloh, where I made my name dwell at first, and see what I did to it because of the evil of my people Israel.
verses.after: ‘Go now to my place at Shiloh, where I first made my name dwell. See what I did to it because of my people Israel’s wickedness.
verses.tsw_comparator: But go now to my place that was in Shiloh, where I made my name dwell at first, and see what I did to it because of the evil of my people Israel.

verses.rationale: Renders rising-early idiom as persistence and keeps both failed responses.
verses.before: And now, because you have done all these things, declares the LORD, and because I spoke to you, rising early and speaking, but you did not listen, and I called to you, but you did not answer,
verses.after: Now, because you have done all these things,’ declares the **LORD**, ‘and because I spoke to you persistently but you did not listen, called you but you did not answer,
verses.tsw_comparator: And now, because you have done all these things, declares the LORD, and because I spoke to you, rising early and speaking, but you did not listen, and I called to you, but you did not answer,

verses.rationale: Preserves threat to both temple and land.
verses.before: I will do to the house that is called by my name, in which you trust, and to the place that I gave to you and to your ancestors, as I did to Shiloh.
verses.after: I will do to the house that bears my name, the house you trust, and to the place I gave you and your ancestors, what I did to Shiloh.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will do to the house that is called by my name, in which you trust, and to the place that I gave to you and to your ancestors, as I did to Shiloh.

verses.rationale: Keeps kinship and northern Israel reference.
verses.before: I will cast you away from before me, as I cast away all your kindred, all the offspring of Ephraim.
verses.after: I will cast you out of my presence, just as I cast out all your brothers, all Ephraim’s offspring.’
verses.tsw_comparator: I will cast you away from before me, as I cast away all your kindred, all the offspring of Ephraim.

verses.rationale: Preserves three prohibitions against prophetic intercession.
verses.before: As for you, do not pray for this people. Do not lift up for them a cry or a prayer, and do not plead with me, for I will not hear you.
verses.after: “As for you, do not pray for this people. Do not raise a cry or prayer for them; do not intercede with me, for I will not listen to you.
verses.tsw_comparator: As for you, do not pray for this people. Do not lift up for them a cry or a prayer, and do not plead with me, for I will not hear you.

verses.rationale: Keeps geographically public scope.
verses.before: Do you not see what they are doing in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem?
verses.after: Do you not see what they are doing in Judah’s cities and Jerusalem’s streets?
verses.tsw_comparator: Do you not see what they are doing in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem?

verses.rationale: Retains whole-household roles and named female deity title.
verses.before: The children gather wood, the fathers kindle the fire, and the women knead dough to make cakes for the queen of heaven; and they pour out drink offerings to other gods, provoking me to anger.
verses.after: The children gather wood, the fathers light the fire, and the women knead dough to make cakes for the Queen of Heaven. They pour drink offerings to other gods to provoke me.
verses.tsw_comparator: The children gather wood, the fathers kindle the fire, and the women knead dough to make cakes for the queen of heaven; and they pour out drink offerings to other gods, provoking me to anger.

verses.rationale: Keeps reflexive consequence framed as questions.
verses.before: Is it I whom they provoke to anger? declares the LORD. Is it not themselves, to the shame of their own faces?
verses.after: Is it me they provoke?” declares the **LORD**. “Is it not themselves, bringing shame upon their own faces?
verses.tsw_comparator: Is it I whom they provoke to anger? declares the LORD. Is it not themselves, to the shame of their own faces?

verses.rationale: Retains nonhuman victims and poured/burning imagery.
verses.before: So thus says the Lord GOD: Look, my anger and my wrath are being poured out on this place—on human beings and animals, on the trees of the field and the fruit of the ground. It will burn and not be quenched.
verses.after: “So this is what the Lord **GOD** says: Look, my anger and fury will pour over this place—over people and animals, over field trees and the ground’s fruit. It will burn and will not be quenched.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore thus says the Lord GOD: Look, my anger and my wrath are being poured out on this place—on human beings and animals, on the trees of the field and the fruit of the ground. It will burn and not be quenched.

verses.rationale: Preserves sarcastic permission to eat what would otherwise be wholly burned.
verses.before: Thus says the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel: Add your burnt offerings to your sacrifices, and eat the flesh.
verses.after: “This is what the **LORD** of hosts, Israel’s God, says: Add your burnt offerings to your other sacrifices and eat the meat!
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus says the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel: Add your burnt offerings to your sacrifices, and eat the flesh.

verses.rationale: Retains categorical wording without inserting merely or primarily to harmonize.
verses.before: For on the day I brought your ancestors out of the land of Egypt, I did not speak with them or command them concerning burnt offering and sacrifice.
verses.after: For when I brought your ancestors out of Egypt, I did not speak to them or command them about burnt offerings and sacrifices.
verses.tsw_comparator: For on the day I brought your ancestors out of the land of Egypt, I did not speak with them or command them concerning burnt offering and sacrifice.

verses.rationale: Keeps covenant formula and obedience linked to welfare.
verses.before: But this is what I commanded them: ‘Listen to my voice, and I will be your God, and you will be my people. Walk in all the way that I command you, so that it may go well with you.’
verses.after: But this is what I commanded them: Listen to my voice, and I will be your God and you will be my people. Walk in every way I command you, so it may go well for you.
verses.tsw_comparator: But this is what I commanded them: ‘Listen to my voice, and I will be your God, and you will be my people. Walk in all the way that I command you, so that it may go well with you.’

verses.rationale: Preserves directional metaphor and double refusal.
verses.before: But they did not listen or incline their ear. They walked in their own counsels, in the stubbornness of their evil heart; they went backward and not forward.
verses.after: Yet they did not listen or incline their ears. They followed their own plans and the stubbornness of their evil hearts; they went backward, not forward.
verses.tsw_comparator: But they did not listen or incline their ear. They walked in their own counsels, in the stubbornness of their evil heart; they went backward and not forward.

verses.rationale: Keeps long duration and repeated sending.
verses.before: From the day your ancestors came out of the land of Egypt until this day, I have sent to you all my servants the prophets, day after day, rising early and sending them.
verses.after: From the day your ancestors left Egypt until today, I have sent you all my servants the prophets, day after day, persistently sending them.
verses.tsw_comparator: From the day your ancestors came out of the land of Egypt until this day, I have sent to you all my servants the prophets, day after day, rising early and sending them.

verses.rationale: Retains body idiom and worsening comparison.
verses.before: Yet they did not listen to me or incline their ear. They stiffened their neck; they acted more wickedly than their ancestors.
verses.after: But they did not listen to me or incline their ears. They stiffened their necks and did worse than their ancestors.
verses.tsw_comparator: Yet they did not listen to me or incline their ear. They stiffened their neck; they acted more wickedly than their ancestors.

verses.rationale: Preserves commanded speech despite predicted refusal.
verses.before: You will speak all these words to them, but they will not listen to you. You will call to them, but they will not answer you.
verses.after: “Tell them all these words, but they will not listen to you. Call to them, but they will not answer you.
verses.tsw_comparator: You will speak all these words to them, but they will not listen to you. You will call to them, but they will not answer you.

verses.rationale: Keeps nation singular and lost faithfulness image.
verses.before: Then you will say to them: This is the nation that has not listened to the voice of the LORD its God and has not accepted discipline. Faithfulness has perished; it has been cut off from their mouth.
verses.after: Say to them: This is the nation that did not listen to the **LORD** its God or accept discipline. Faithfulness has perished; it has been cut off from their mouths.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then you will say to them: This is the nation that has not listened to the voice of the LORD its God and has not accepted discipline. Faithfulness has perished; it has been cut off from their mouth.

verses.rationale: Preserves female city mourning commands and cut hair.
verses.before: Cut off your consecrated hair and throw it away; raise a lament on the bare heights. For the LORD has rejected and abandoned the generation of his wrath.
verses.after: Cut off your hair and throw it away; raise a lament on the bare heights, for the **LORD** has rejected and abandoned the generation that aroused his wrath.
verses.tsw_comparator: Cut off your consecrated hair and throw it away; raise a lament on the bare heights. For the LORD has rejected and abandoned the generation of his wrath.

verses.rationale: Keeps concrete temple defilement.
verses.before: For the people of Judah have done what is evil in my eyes, declares the LORD. They have set their detestable things in the house that is called by my name, defiling it.
verses.after: “For the people of Judah have done evil in my eyes,” declares the **LORD**. “They have placed their offensive things in the house that bears my name, defiling it.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the people of Judah have done what is evil in my eyes, declares the LORD. They have set their detestable things in the house that is called by my name, defiling it.

verses.rationale: Preserves both genders of child victims and categorical divine rejection.
verses.before: They have built the high places of Topheth, which is in the Valley of Ben-hinnom, to burn their sons and their daughters in the fire—something I did not command, nor did it enter my heart.
verses.after: They built Topheth’s high places in the Valley of Ben-hinnom to burn their sons and daughters in fire—something I did not command and that never entered my mind.
verses.tsw_comparator: They have built the high places of Topheth, which is in the Valley of Ben-hinnom, to burn their sons and their daughters in the fire—something I did not command, nor did it enter my heart.

verses.rationale: Keeps renamed valley and lack of burial space elsewhere as the reason for burial at Topheth.
verses.before: So, look, days are coming, declares the LORD, when it will no longer be called Topheth or the Valley of Ben-hinnom, but the Valley of Slaughter. They will bury in Topheth because there is no other place.
verses.after: So look, days are coming,” declares the **LORD**, “when it will no longer be called Topheth or the Valley of Ben-hinnom, but the Valley of Slaughter. They will bury people at Topheth for lack of room elsewhere.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore, look, days are coming, declares the LORD, when it will no longer be called Topheth or the Valley of Ben-hinnom, but the Valley of Slaughter. They will bury in Topheth because there is no other place.

verses.rationale: Retains exposed dead and unimpeded scavengers.
verses.before: The corpses of this people will become food for the birds of the heavens and for the animals of the earth, with no one to frighten them away.
verses.after: The corpses of this people will become food for the birds of the heavens and the animals of the earth, with no one to frighten them away.
verses.tsw_comparator: The corpses of this people will become food for the birds of the heavens and for the animals of the earth, with no one to frighten them away.

verses.rationale: Preserves four joy/voice terms ending in destroyed land.
verses.before: I will bring to an end from the cities of Judah and from the streets of Jerusalem the sound of rejoicing and the sound of gladness, the voice of groom and the voice of bride; for the land will become a wasteland.
verses.after: I will silence in Judah’s cities and Jerusalem’s streets the sound of joy and gladness, the voice of bridegroom and bride, for the land will become a ruin.”
verses.tsw_comparator: I will bring to an end from the cities of Judah and from the streets of Jerusalem the sound of rejoicing and the sound of gladness, the voice of groom and the voice of bride; for the land will become a wasteland.

comparative_references.scope: All 207 TSW verses read after independent drafting from each selected Hebrew record and all annotations. Shared wording retained where clear; overlap is triage only.
